outcome: No case of the classical Bass–Quillen conjecture (vector bundles / f.g. projective modules over a regular Noetherian ring A vs. A[t1,...,tn]) was settled in the window; the two 2025 papers found generalize the conjecture to torsors/G-bundles and to non-Noetherian valuation rings, which are related problems rather than restrictions of the stated conjecture.
summary: The classical Bass–Quillen conjecture states that for a regular Noetherian ring A, every finitely generated projective A[t1,...,tn]-module is extended from A (equivalently, every vector bundle on affine space over Spec A descends to Spec A). Two papers found in the triage pass, both from 2025, address generalizations of this conjecture rather than the conjecture itself. (1) Guo–Liu, 'The Bass–Quillen conjecture for torsors over valuation rings' (arXiv:2503.10163, submitted 2025-03-13, published in IMRN 2025) prove a descent result for reductive-group torsors over smooth algebras A over a valuation ring V. Fetching the paper confirms that valuation rings (in particular non-Noetherian Prüfer rings) fall outside the classical conjecture's hypothesis of a regular Noetherian base ring, and the authors frame mixed-characteristic, non-Noetherian settings as a genuinely new regime rather than a restriction of the classical statement. This is a related problem under §3.1 (same name, different objects/rings), not a case of the stated conjecture. (2) Stavrova, 'On the generalized Bass–Quillen conjecture in dimension 2' (arXiv:2512.18868, submitted 2025-12-21) proves the dimension-≤-2 case for principal G-bundles for reductive groups G with split semisimple derived group. Fetching the paper shows it explicitly states that specializing to G=GL_n recovers the *classical* dimension-≤-2 case, which the authors attribute to Murthy (n=1) and to Suslin/Quillen (general n) — i.e., already known well before the window. Stavrova's new contribution is restricted to other reductive groups (not GL_n), so it extends the generalized conjecture rather than adding new territory to the classical vector-bundle statement Wikipedia poses. Neither paper settles, refines, or contradicts anything about the classical Bass–Quillen conjecture as such; no counterexample, no new case, and no bound on file. The Wikipedia article's own text (fetched) lists the state of the art as Lindel (1981, smooth k-algebras) and Asok–Hoyois–Wendt (2018, homotopy-invariance results) and does not mention any post-2024 development, consistent with what direct searches turned up. No source of any kind — in either paper, in secondary commentary, or in general searches for AI and this conjecture — mentions any AI system, machine-learning tool, or automated theorem prover contributing to any of this work; both papers read as traditional human mathematics with no AI acknowledgement of any kind.
competing_reading: One could argue Stavrova's dimension-2 G-bundle theorem is 'progress' on a generalized version of Bass–Quillen that Wikipedia's bullet doesn't explicitly separate from the classical one, since Wikipedia's own phrasing just says 'vector bundles' without foreclosing the torsor generalization by name. But the statement given names vector bundles over A and A[t1,...,tn] specifically, and both new papers' own contributions lie strictly outside that (either different objects — G-torsors for G ≠ GL_n — or a different ring class — non-Noetherian valuation rings), so under §3.1's test ('does this change what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry?') the answer is no.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving a new case of the classical conjecture for GL_n vector bundles over a regular Noetherian ring not already covered by Lindel/Popescu/Murthy/Suslin/Quillen, or a counterexample to the general conjecture, would change this record's status.
